title: Why we built Yardsort
description: The decisions behind Yardsort: parallel coding on Linux, macOS and Windows, real agent terminals, and workspaces you can inspect with git.

title: What git worktrees solve—and what they don’t—for parallel coding agents
description: Git worktrees separate working files and branches. Learn why parallel coding agents still need dependency setup, separate ports and integration tests.

title: Yardsort vs Superset
description: Compare Yardsort and Superset for parallel coding agents: desktop platforms, local and remote workspaces, review tools, session persistence and costs.

title: Yardsort vs Conductor
description: Compare Yardsort’s local desktop workflow with Conductor’s Mac and cloud workspaces, including agent choice, review tools, pricing and data handling.

title: Run Claude Code and Codex in parallel with git worktrees
description: Use Yardsort to give Claude Code and Codex separate tasks, prepare their worktrees, review each diff and open two focused pull requests.
